justification: Adds a one-letter OCR repair to scripts/state_law_recopy.py words_dropped, so a state-law row that is the law's own words with one misread letter ('parkin' for 'parking') can be re-copied. Measured over the 57 unproven state rows: clears exactly 1 (38711, Codes SEPP 3D.46(10), served on the address check page by app/api/sepp/exempt-complying). Re-copied live with the existing guarded apply script; DQ-145 98 -> 97, ceiling lowered.

falsifiable_check.fails_when: Replacing the new branch's condition with False: 1 failed / 23 passed (test_one_letter_ocr_slip_is_a_repair_not_a_dropped_word). Clean: 24 passed.
falsifiable_check.observed_red: Measured 2026-10-19 by sed-ing the condition to `if False:` and running the file: 1 failed, 23 passed.
falsifiable_check.external_authority: The in-force Codes SEPP (epi-2008-0572 snapshot 2026-10-16): the new text of 38711 is unit sec.3D.46-ssec.10, verbatim in the law by both provers (check a).

pre_impl.existing_data: words_dropped already forgave ligature losses and a row cut off mid-word at its end; test_cut_off_word_in_the_middle_is_not_forgiven ('Poo' for 'Pools') must still fail, and does (two letters).
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: Expected the rule to clear several state rows; measured it clears 1 of 57. The 4 rows failing only on dropped words hold real extra words ('and', 'an', 'zone', 'or 2'), not slips, and stay refused.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: One helper (one_letter_slip) and one branch in the existing replace handling. No new query; apply path unchanged.

functions.name: one_letter_slip
functions.input: a row word and the law word it replaces, one-for-one
functions.output: True only for exactly one letter added, dropped or changed, law word 4+ letters, no digits
functions.if_none: not applicable: returns bool; False keeps the old behaviour (word counted as dropped, row refused)

functions.name: words_dropped
functions.input: the row text and the unit's words
functions.output: words of the row not in the unit; one-letter slips now listed in repairs instead
functions.if_none: empty list means every row word is explained

break_it.scenario: A changed number passes as a one-letter slip (1.8 vs 1.9).
break_it.what_happens: A different rule would be treated as the same.
break_it.how: Words with any digit never match; check d also requires every old number in the new text.

break_it.scenario: Short words with different meaning (of/or, may/many).
break_it.what_happens: The row could be matched to the wrong unit.
break_it.how: Law word must be 4+ letters; the written text is always the law's unit, never the row's words.
break_it.repro: python -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'scripts'); import state_law_recopy as R; print(R.one_letter_slip('of','or'))"

break_it.scenario: A two-letter loss in the middle of the row is forgiven.
break_it.what_happens: A row missing words would be re-copied as if whole.
break_it.how: Only a one-for-one swap at edit distance 1; the existing 'Poo'/'Pools' test still fails as intended.

real_layer_exempt.scripts/state_law_recopy.py: The changed functions are pure text matching; no database or HTTP call was added. The live write used the existing apply_state_law_recopy.py (md5, current, version-history and rowcount guards, backup committed).

residual_risk: A one-letter plural change (storey/storeys) now counts as a slip for UNIT CHOICE only; the stored text becomes the law's own words, so no wrong wording can be served. 56 state rows remain unproven.

post_merge.db_reset: No. The single live re-copy (38711) is already applied; backup data/db_rollback_backups/state_law_recopy_pre_2026-10-19T110955.json.
post_merge.manual_verify: python scripts/dq_probe_live.py --id DQ-145 prints 97 or lower.
